channel.title: Safearly blog
channel.description: Essays, research notes and explainers on fast, safe AI in production.

item.title: Weight-space programming, explained: when an LLM edits a neural network's weights
item.description: In November 2026 MIT CSAIL researchers showed a frontier LLM reading and rewriting another network's weights directly, with no training loop. What weight-space programming is, what the experiments showed, the caveats, and why it matters for auditing and AI safety.

item.title: The agent security stack is taking shape: sandboxes, policy engines and credential brokers
item.description: October 2026 brought open-source agent sandboxes with policy engines and credential brokers that keep passwords away from agents. How the new layers fit together, and what's still missing.

item.title: Agent Skills is now an open standard. Here's what it means for security
item.description: Anthropic donated Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation in October 2026, with hundreds of millions of skill installs across more than 70 platforms. What a shared standard changes, and the security practices every team installing skills should adopt now.

item.title: Permission-aware retrieval: why filtering the answer is too late
item.description: An AI assistant must apply access control before the model reads anything. How permission-aware retrieval works, why filtering answers afterwards fails, and how to test it.

item.title: Running a private AI assistant on one GPU
item.description: A practical guide to self-hosting an AI assistant on a single consumer graphics card: how memory is spent, which models fit, and the tricks that matter most, starting with not calling the model at all.

item.title: Prompt injection, explained with one example
item.description: What prompt injection is, why indirect injection through web pages and documents is the dangerous kind, why detection alone can't stop it, and the design rule that does: approval for actions after reading outside content.

item.title: RAG, explained for people who have to trust the answer
item.description: Retrieval-augmented generation in plain language: chunking, indexing, hybrid search, reranking, citations and verification, and the questions to ask before you trust an answer from one.

item.title: An agent should never know more than the person asking
item.description: Most enterprise agents run on a service account that can read everything. That turns every shared assistant, chat bot and widget into a way around access control. A design where the agent always acts as the person asking.

item.title: Agents or workflows? How to choose
item.description: An agent decides what to do; a workflow follows a process you drew. A practical guide to picking one, with examples, and why most teams end up using both.

item.title: Check every sentence, not just the answer
item.description: A citation at the end of an answer proves little. Checking each sentence against the passage it cites, numbers included, and refusing to show what fails, is how retrieval answers become something people can act on.

item.title: Smriti now does workflows and lives where your team works
item.description: Release notes: visual workflows with human approval, a website widget, Slack, Telegram and Discord bots, and the safety rules that come with them.

item.title: Guardrails have a latency budget
item.description: A guardrail that adds noticeable latency gets switched off. How to design guardrails fast enough to run on every request and inside the stream, with measured numbers.

item.title: Least privilege for agent skills
item.description: Multipurpose agents load skills and tools from strangers. A skill should declare what it needs, get nothing more, and leave a record. A design for secure agent skills.

item.title: Where inference time and money actually go
item.description: Prefill is compute-bound, decode is memory-bound, and most serving waste hides in between. A field guide to the inference optimizations that hold up: continuous batching, paged KV cache, speculative decoding and disaggregation.

item.title: Agents need a firewall
item.description: Prompt injection is admitted to be unsolved. In every major agent leak of the past year, the data left through a legitimate tool call. That is where the guardrail belongs.

item.title: A checksum is not enough: detecting Indian PII in the real world
item.description: About one random 12-digit number in ten passes the Aadhaar checksum. Why detecting Indian personal data needs labels, scripts and OCR repair, and what today's tools do.

item.title: India's AI trust rulebook, for builders
item.description: DPDP, the Aadhaar Data Vault, CERT-In, RBI's FREE-AI and the IT Rules: what is in force, what is draft, and what it means for your LLM app, as of October 2026.
